subject: Volume coverage & settlement mechanics for hosted API commit
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@borealis.com>
Cc: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@borealis.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Volume coverage & settlement mechanics for hosted API commit

Hi Elena / Matt,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — great alignment on the integration milestones. Per our conversation, I wanted to outline the proposed mechanics for the Hosted API commit and how quarterly/annual settlement would work so your finance team can review. High level:

- Commit tier: Borealis would commit to 18B tokens / year (split by quarter for cadence planning). Pricing reflects per-token discounts at that commit level; details in the attached draft terms (Redwood-Commit-Terms-v3.pdf).
- True-up cadence options we support: quarterly true-up (recommended for most customers) or annual true-up (possible with upfront prepay).
- Quarterly true-up flow (option suggested):
  1) At the end of each quarter we compare actual usage to the committed pro-rata amount for the quarter.
  2) If usage > pro-rata, overage is billed at the overage rate shown in the SOW (usually the committed unit price) and appears on the next invoice.
  3) If usage < pro-rata, we can either issue a credit (make-good) to be applied to the next quarter or invoice the shortfall depending on the option you select.

Key negotiation points to confirm from your side: make-good cap (we typically see anywhere from no cap to a 20% cap per quarter), whether credits can be carried forward beyond one quarter, and whether Borealis prefers invoice-based shortfall settlement versus credit first. Also confirming reporting cadence — we can provide weekly usage exports and a final reconciled report at quarter close.

Attached: my suggested language and a usage projection file you asked for. If it helps, I can put together two redline options for your GC/finance: (A) quarterly true-up with credits carryforward up to one quarter, (B) annual true-up with no carryforward but a one-time annual true-up invoice.

Next steps: please let me know which cadence you prefer and any constraints from procurement (e.g., PO timing, internal approval windows). Happy to hop on a short call with your finance team next week.

Thanks,
Sooj
--

Subject: Re: Volume coverage & settlement mechanics for hosted API commit

Hi Sooj — thanks for the write-up and the projection. A couple clarifying Qs from our side before we loop in procurement: 

1) For the quarterly true-up, if we under-use the pro-rata amount and elect to take a credit (make-good), does that credit reduce our committed baseline going forward or is it purely a billing offset?
2) If we do an annual true-up, what happens mid-year if we spike above the pro-rata? Is there an interim billing process or temporary overage pricing?

Also — we have one internal requirement: credits must be usable for at least two quarters (finance policy) or else we need the contract to allow invoice settlement. Would Redwood be flexible on a two-quarter carryforward?

Matt and I will review the draft terms and mark up the places that affect accounting. If you can provide the explicit examples (math) for a quarterly example and an annual example with an identical usage pattern, that would help speed things up.

Elena
Elena Park
Director, Finance — Borealis, Inc.
elena.park@borealis.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@borealis.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@borealis.com>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 08:52:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Volume coverage & settlement mechanics for hosted API commit

Thanks, Elena — good questions. Quick answers and I'll follow up with a worked example attachment.

1) Credits (make-goods): default approach is that credits are a billing offset (reduce future invoices) and do not reduce the committed baseline unless explicitly agreed in the SOW. So your committed quantity stays intact unless we document a permanent reduction.

2) Annual true-up with mid-year spikes: we support interim overage billing. If you spike above pro-rata mid-year, overages are billed monthly/quarterly at the agreed overage rate; the year-end true-up reconciles to the annual commit and any remaining shortfalls/overages are settled then.

Regarding your two-quarter carryforward requirement: Redwood is generally flexible on carryforward up to two quarters for deals of this size; the trade-offs we typically see are (a) longer carryforward increases variability in resource planning, and (b) we sometimes include a limited cap on carryforward (e.g., credits cannot exceed 25% of the quarterly pro-rata). If that sounds acceptable I can draft that into Option A and send to procurement.

I'll attach a worked example showing: committed pro-rata per quarter, scenario A (steady under-use), scenario B (spike then drop), and how credits vs invoice settlement plays out.

Sooj
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: recommended guardrails for Borealis commit

Internal notes for Sooj / Vanessa — copying language we prefer to propose to Borealis so procurement reviewers see a clear default: 

- Quarterly true-up is our recommended default for hosted customers unless they insist on annual.
- Carryforward: allow credits to carry forward up to 2 quarters; credits > 25% of quarter pro-rata must be approved by Sales Ops.
- Make-good cap: suggest a soft cap of 30% per quarter (negotiable).
- Invoice vs credit: default to credit first, invoice for remaining shortfall after credits expire or if customer requests invoice settlement.
- Reporting: weekly usage exports + final reconciled CSV at quarter close (attachment: 20260531-usage-export.csv).

If Borealis insists on annual true-up, recommend requiring a mid-year alert threshold (70% of annual commit) to trigger a review and optional interim invoicing for overages > 15% of pro-rata.

Aditya
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@borealis.com>
Cc: Matt O'Neill <matt.oneill@borealis.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Volume coverage & settlement mechanics for hosted API commit

Elena / Matt — attaching the worked examples and a redline we think matches your two-quarter carryforward ask (see Redwood-Commit-Terms-v3.pdf). Summary of the proposed settlement terms: 

- Commit: 18B tokens / year, billed at committed discounted unit price.
- Quarterly true-up (default): reconcile each quarter vs pro-rata. Credits issued for under-use and can be carried forward up to 2 quarters; credits capped at 25% of quarterly pro-rata without Sales Ops approval.
- Overage: billed at committed overage rate; interim bills can be issued if usage > 115% of pro-rata in a single month.
- Annual true-up (alternate): final reconciliation at year end; if selected, include mid-year review at 70% of annual run-rate.

If that framing works, I'll send the SOW redline and DocuSign link to your procurement contact. We can also add a short clause about audit/reporting: Redwood will provide weekly exports and a reconciled CSV at quarter close; Borealis retains the right to request a one-time audit of usage in case of a billing dispute.

Would you like procurement to sign the redline or do you want one more pass from finance? Happy to set a 30-minute call with procurement tomorrow.

Thanks,
Sooj

Attachments: Redwood-Commit-Terms-v3.pdf, borealis-usage-proj-q2-2026.xlsx, 20260531-usage-export.csv
